— E-commerce

Make buying feel straightforward.

An online store needs more than attractive product pages. I help connect catalogue organization, customer information, technical setup, and marketing so that people can find, assess, and buy what you sell.

Discuss e-commerce

A connected approach to e-commerce

E-commerce work involves decisions across the whole shopping journey. Categories must reflect how customers browse; product information must reduce uncertainty; shipping, returns, and payment details must be clear before checkout. Marketing should lead people to the right destination, and measurement should distinguish browsing from completed purchases. A store project brings these pieces together within the capabilities of the chosen platform.

When this work can help

  • Customers struggle to find products or compare relevant options.
  • Product and category pages lack important buying information.
  • Store marketing and purchase tracking provide conflicting views of performance.

How I approach the work

I review the catalogue, customer journeys, platform, operational constraints, and available data. The work is prioritized around the largest sources of confusion or technical friction. Design and development decisions account for product variants, stock handling, payment integrations, and the people maintaining the store. Measurement is planned before significant changes go live.

Core activities & deliverables

Store architecture

Plan categories, navigation, filtering, product URL behavior, and useful internal links. Consider search visibility without generating large numbers of thin or duplicate pages.

Product and checkout journey

Improve product templates, essential buying details, trust information, and mobile usability. Review checkout constraints and third-party payment flows within the platform limits.

Marketing and measurement

Connect relevant landing pages with SEO, advertising, and content. Define purchase events, product identifiers, and transaction deduplication, then verify the actual flow before using reports for budget decisions.

Who this is for

This work suits businesses planning a new online store, reorganizing a growing catalogue, or improving an established shopping journey. Requirements depend on the products, fulfillment process, markets actually served, and platform. The business remains responsible for accurate product claims, stock, pricing, shipping terms, tax obligations, and customer service; those operational foundations should be understood before design begins.

What to consider before starting

Platform capabilities, payment providers, consent, browser restrictions, and operational issues can constrain what is possible. I do not guarantee sales growth or a specific conversion rate. Custom integrations may require specialist work, additional access, and separate testing. Product feeds and campaign eligibility also depend on platform policy and the accuracy of the underlying business information.

How we assess progress

Review the path from product discovery through checkout, including where customers stop and whether recorded purchases match actual orders. Revenue reporting should account for cancellations and refunds where the available systems support it. A useful improvement plan distinguishes traffic quality, store usability, pricing, and fulfillment issues rather than attributing every problem to the website design.

Questions about e-commerce

Which store platform should I use?+

Choose based on catalogue complexity, payment and fulfillment needs, editing workflow, integrations, and ongoing cost. The platform decision follows requirements rather than a universal preference.

Can marketing be included?+

SEO, advertising, content, and measurement can support a store engagement. Their scope and costs should be agreed separately from the build requirements.
